**FIX A (r07 Pattern B3 — first_value / last_value / nth_value default-frame footgun)**: Trino HAS `first_value`, `last_value`, `nth_value` as value-window functions, but the DEFAULT frame is `RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` (per [trino.io/docs/current/functions/window.html](https://trino.io/docs/current/functions/window.html), confirmed via WebSearch). So `last_value(x) OVER (PARTITION BY p ORDER BY o)` returns the CURRENT row's value (frame ends at current row's peer group, NOT partition end), not the partition's true last value. Fix requires explicit `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING`. WebSearch nuance noted: under default RANGE frame, frame_end CURRENT ROW means last PEER (rows with same ORDER BY value); when ORDER BY has unique values the last peer IS the current row. Canonical handles both cases.

**FIX B (r27 §6.7G — dbt var() three-piece pattern for per-run configurable values)**: The real configurable-value mechanism is dbt `var()` + `vars:` block + `--vars` CLI, NOT `{% set %}`. Confirmed via WebSearch at docs.getdbt.com/reference/dbt-jinja-functions/var + docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/project-variables: var('name', default) is the function (default fires when var not defined); top-level `vars:` block in dbt_project.yml holds defaults; `--vars` CLI flag (plural, YAML dict) overrides at run time. Precedence: --vars > project vars > var() default arg.
